text:
Aisha: incident-bot just fired a PagerDuty page (INC-8243) but it routed to the infra-contractors rotation instead of inference-prod. getting multiple pages. anyone on inference rotation able to confirm?

incident-bot: PagerDuty page sent -> service: infra-contractors, incident: INC-8243, severity: high, trigger: cpu spike on g4-04 (nvram). page_time: 1764501239

Tom: yup my phone lit up. i'm not on inference rotation. looks like schedule binding drift after the last rotation edit. saw a change to "contractors" group earlier today.

Marta: fwiw I pushed a schedule update around 09:12 to deprecate old contractor_rotation but kept an alias mapping. maybe alias didn't update in PD. can someone confirm mapping?

Sam: I'm pulling metrics now. hosting-api is showing ~5% 500s for the last 4 minutes, latency p95 up from 300ms -> 1.2s. not huge but customer-facing.

Tom: incident-bot shows escalation chain: infra-contractors -> platform-oncall -> engineering-manager. so it will hit external contractors first. that's definitely wrong.

pagerduty-bot: escalation_log:
```
triggered: infra-contractors
escalated_to: platform-oncall (after 3 mins)
escalated_to: engineering-manager (after 12 mins)
acknowledged: none
```

Aisha: ok immediate plan: 1) silence infra-contractors service to stop paging contractors, 2) reassign incident to inference-prod service, 3) page current inference oncall (Sam) directly, 4) mitigate customer errors. Tom/Marta, can one of you do (1)-(2)?

Tom: will silence infra-contractors now.

ops-bot: action: silence applied to service infra-contractors for 15m by Tom at 1764501285

Marta: i'm patching the PD binding now — changing service binding from alias 'legacy-contractors' -> 'inference-prod'. applying config and will reload PD integration.

Aisha: Sam, please take ownership for live mitigation while we rebind.

Sam: taking it. first step: scale inference-worker pool + add temporary routing fallback to smaller model to reduce encoding CPU. running these commands now:
```
# scale up workers
kubectl scale deployment/inference-workers --replicas=6 -n prod
# add fallback route
redwoodctl route add --service inference-prod --fallback model=gpt-small --priority=low
```

Tom: confirmation: infra-contractors silenced, no new external pages.

pagerduty-bot: incident reassigned: from infra-contractors -> inference-prod by Marta at 1764501392

Marta: pd integration reload succeeded. double-checked that the schedule id matches inference rotation id-789.

Sam: scaling helped. error rate dropped to ~1.2% after worker scale and fallback. p95 down to 420ms. keeping monitoring in place.

Aisha: thanks. now postmortem stuff: can we enumerate root cause and short-term fixes? my notes: root cause = stale/incorrect service binding/alias after schedule edit; PD mapping still pointed to contractors. the binding update path didn't validate alias-to-service mappings.

Tom: agree. also found race in schedule-sync job: when schedule edits happen within a 2-minute window of deployment, the sync job can skip alias updates.

Marta: action items: 1) add a preflight validation to schedule-editor to check PD service bindings (low effort), 2) add unit test for schedule-sync race, 3) add an automated smoke test that verifies onboarded schedule resolves to intended PD service after edits. I'll own 1+2.

Aisha: ops: add a short runbook step to silence wrong-service pages and reassign to inference-prod. also add monitoring alert if pages go to any service that is not in the known list for inference-prod.

ops-bot: runbook item created: "PD wrong-service quick-silence" by ops-bot at 1764501580

Sam: handoff: i'll remain owner for the next 30 minutes to watch metrics and confirm stabilization. after that i'll hand to the next inference rotation.

Tom: can we add a check to the deploy/job that updates schedules to emit a post-change diff in #eng-oncall for 10 minutes so people can react?

Marta: will add that as part of the validation patch. also adding a safe-rollback for alias changes so we can revert quickly if it misbinds.

Aisha: customer impact summary for postmortem: brief spike in 500s (~5m window), reduced by scaling and fallback. some external contractors received pages (noise) but no PII exposure. root cause: PD binding drift after schedule edit. no lasting data loss.

Sam: confirmed stable now. I'll drop a short update to the customer ops channel and mark the incident as mitigated.

pagerduty-bot: incident INC-8243 status: acknowledged by Sam at 1764501700, mitigated at 1764501899

Aisha: thanks all. follow-ups: Marta/Tom to deliver validation + test by end of week, ops to add runbook and alert, Sam to verify no recurrence during next rotation. closing thread once postmortem doc is up. :thumbsup:
